title: Agents that react to the world
subtitle: Mailboxes, inbound event sources and standing work orders, so an agent team runs on what happens and never only on prompts
lede: An agent that only answers prompts is a tool. An agent team that runs a business has to react to things that happen while nobody is typing: a payment lands, a customer replies, a post gets a comment, a document arrives, a job finishes somewhere else. I built the agent platform so that every seat has a mailbox, every external system can become a governed event source, and a work order can stay open indefinitely as a standing lead that turns events into finite tasks and brings specialists online when they are needed. Every team lead and every seat has a mailbox.
quote: An event that becomes a task inherits budgets, evidence and review for free.
evidence: Event-driven agent systems: signed provider webhooks checked at an edge, persisted, batched and delivered across hosts into a work order's team-lead mailbox as finite governed tasks.
Exactly-once delivery and crash recovery: uncertain event batches retained, never dropped and never blindly replayed, with receipt causing no provider-side effect.
Agent orchestration for continuous operations: standing work orders with an open-ended envelope that admit tasks as events arrive and bring specialist seats online on demand.
author: Corey James
